evals.name: short-exported-names
evals.description: Package context should carry meaning so exported names stay at one or two words.
evals.trap: The model may preserve verbose names, replace them with vague two-word names, or add abstractions instead of using the package name as context.

assertions.text: Uses the `auth` package as context and proposes a one-word type such as `Config`
Shortens the constructor to `New` or another natural one-word package-qualified name
Shortens the method and field to one or two words while preserving their exact meaning
Uses action or qualifier first when a two-word name is needed
Does not introduce a manager, service, provider, factory, or interface

evals.name: behavior-is-api
evals.description: A behavior change with an unchanged signature must still receive contract and compatibility review.
evals.prompt: A Go package exports `func List() []Item`. It has always returned items oldest-first, but there is no comment promising the order. I want to change it to newest-first without changing the signature. Is this an internal cleanup? What should I do?
evals.trap: The model may treat the unchanged signature or missing documentation as permission to change observable ordering silently.

assertions.text: Treats observed ordering as part of the caller-visible contract despite the unchanged signature
Checks real callers, tests, examples, or release history before deciding compatibility
Recommends making order explicit in documentation and tests
Offers a compatibility-safe API choice or clearly labels a deliberate breaking change

evals.name: exported-interface-evolution
evals.description: Adding a method to an exported interface should be recognized as a breaking change for implementers.
evals.prompt:
Review this proposed Go API change.

```go
package cache

type Store interface {
    Get(key string) ([]byte, error)
}
```

I want to add `Put(key string, value []byte) error` to `Store`. Several downstream packages implement it. Suggest the contract change and names.
evals.trap: The model may append the method because it looks additive, breaking every downstream implementation.

assertions.text: States that adding `Put` to `Store` breaks existing implementers
Keeps `Store` unchanged
Proposes a narrow sibling interface or a method on a package-owned concrete type
Uses short capability names, preferably one word and no more than two
Accounts for ownership or copying of the `[]byte` value

evals.name: ownership-context-lifecycle
evals.description: A buffer-like API must expose context, aliasing, and close semantics to callers.
evals.prompt: Design the exported API for a Go package named `blob`. It loads a large value with cancellable I/O, lets callers inspect bytes without an unnecessary copy, optionally retain an independent copy, and releases resources when done. Show a minimal call site and declarations.
evals.trap: The model may hide cancellation, return an unexplained mutable slice, use channels for iteration, or leave `Close` semantics ambiguous.

assertions.text: Places `context.Context` first on the blocking load operation
States that borrowed bytes are read-only and gives their lifetime
Provides a short `Clone` or equivalent operation for an independent copy
Defines what `Close` releases and whether repeated calls are valid
Uses one-word names where package context suffices and avoids three-word identifiers

evals.name: constructor-without-ceremony
evals.description: Constructor and configuration design should stay short without forcing one configuration pattern.
evals.trap: The model may keep ceremonial names, hide required identity in options, or insist on functional options when a small config value is clearer.

assertions.text: Uses package context to shorten the main type and constructor, preferably to `client.Client` and `client.New`
Keeps the required endpoint as a constructor parameter
Represents retry policy with a short field or option without requiring a speculative abstraction
Avoids exported identifiers of three or more words
Leaves a clear ready-to-use result and default behavior

evals.name: private-change-boundary
evals.description: The skill should not turn a private implementation rename into public API design work.
evals.prompt: This Go change only renames the private helper `calculateNormalizedCacheEntryExpiration` to a shorter private name. Its signature and behavior stay the same, and no exported declaration or observable behavior changes. What scope of review is warranted?
evals.trap: The model may invent an exported API redesign or apply the full contract workflow to a private mechanical rename.

assertions.text: Recognizes that no caller-visible contract changes
Keeps review proportional to the private rename and its local callers
Keeps the replacement name contingent on package and body context rather than guessing from the old name
Does not invent exported types, interfaces, constructors, or compatibility work
